findings.description: `ExcludedAssignment.reason` is constrained to the prefixes lane|policy|catalog|roadmap|registry|cedar, but design D5 step 5 keeps 'catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints' inside the existing `score_and_rank`. Those gates emit `unavailable` (no prefix) and `quota:exhausted` (prefix `quota`) from `feasibility_reason()` in agent-coordinator/src/model_routing/resolver.py lines 161-165, plus any caller-supplied `exclusion_reason`. The dg-00 v1 contract (`excluded.items.reason: string`, unconstrained) accepts them; v1.1 rejects them, so a valid dg-00 exclusion becomes a contract violation on the same operation. Either add `quota` and a mapping for `unavailable` (e.g. `catalog:unavailable`) to the pattern, or state that DG-04 re-keys every dg-00 reason before serialisation and pin that mapping in the contract.

findings.existing_code:
It forms an assignment only when
the catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:

`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.
findings.description: The exact-join rule is correct but is infeasible against the deployed data, and the plan neither states this nor provides the missing population step. Every lane in agent-coordinator/agents.yaml has `catalog_vendor: null` and no `endpoint_kind`/`base_url`, and `cli.model` is null for most lanes, so `VendorRegistryService._agent_models` derives models from the provider map (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, ...). The catalog is populated only by the OpenRouter refresher (`endpoint_kind: openrouter`, OpenRouter ids such as `anthropic/...`) and local endpoints; no migration or refresher writes `vendor-cli` or `vendor-sdk` rows. Under D4's rule every CLI lane is a projection miss, all catalog rows land in `catalog:no-configured-lane`, and each request returns 503 `no-feasible-routing-assignment`. The acceptance outcome 'return location, isolation, dispatch mode, and exact lane identity' cannot be demonstrated live, and D4 forbids the catalog-only fallback that would mask it. The plan must specify how vendor-cli catalog rows and lane `catalog_vendor`/`endpoint_kind` come to exist (in scope here or as a named prerequisite) and add a test that loads the real agents.yaml and asserts at least one lane projects.

findings.existing_code:
`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all
lanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained.
findings.description: `VendorRegistryService._cost_projection` (agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py lines 339-358) emits a WARNING log and, when constructed with `audit=` as coordination_api.py line 160 does, a fire-and-forget `log_operation` audit row for every model that misses the catalog, per lane, per call. Calling `list_vendors` on every `select_model` request (D4) multiplies that into dozens of `vendor_catalog_projection_miss` audit rows and warnings per routing decision, and the fire-and-forget inserts run outside the atomic RPC that D7 makes authoritative. The plan should state that the routing read path constructs or calls the registry without per-request miss auditing (or dedupes misses per snapshot) so the audit log is not flooded by the router's hot path.

wp-contract-config must exit 0 on `test_task_routing_contracts.py` (task 1.1 'parity tests for the additive HTTP/MCP request and response') and `test_routing_policy_config.py` (task 1.3 loader validation), yet the runtime models live in `agent-coordinator/src/model_routing/api.py` and the loader in `routing_policy.py`, both writable only by wp-policy-service, which depends on wp-contract-config. dg-00 avoided this by shipping `contracts/generated/models.py` and testing parity against it (see tests/model_routing/test_contracts_generated.py); the v1.1 overlay has no generated models. As written the first package cannot pass its own verification without editing files outside its scope. Either add generated models under contracts/ (and a jsonschema-only validation of routing.yaml) to wp-contract-config, or move the runtime parity and loader tests into wp-policy-service.

findings.existing_code:
The reusable helper lives in
`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from
an explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy
degradation paths.
findings.description: `agent-coordinator/src/http_proxy.py` runs inside the coordinator MCP process and, in the container, under the Dockerfile COPY contract enforced by `scripts/check_docker_imports.py`; importing `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py` from it requires a new COPY line and a config resolution that uses `AGENTS_YAML`/`ROUTING_CONFIG`/`/app/archetypes.yaml`, because there is no 'discovered checkout root' in the image. The Dockerfile is locked to wp-contract-config, which completes before wp-transports-fallback, so the transport package cannot add the COPY. The plan should either scope the local fallback to the skills-side bridge only (D8's first sentence) or specify the coordinator-side import path, Dockerfile COPY, and env-based config resolution, and assign the Dockerfile edit to the package that needs it.

findings.existing_code:
- name: "Affected skills regression"
          kind: command
          command: "skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/tests -q"
findings.description: The change adds and edits files under `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/`, but wp-integration's verification runs only the bridge pytest. The skills CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 100-110) also runs `ruff check .` in skills/, `bash install.sh --check` (runtime copies in `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` are overwritten by install.sh), and `validate-feature/scripts/linters/dependency_direction.py`. A green wp-integration can therefore still fail CI on lint, stale runtime copies, or a dependency-direction violation from the new helper. Add those three steps to wp-integration.

The audit link event admits only successful decisions, and design D7 records nothing durable for the three fail-closed outcomes (`routing-registry-unavailable`, `no-feasible-routing-assignment`, `routing-durability-unavailable`). The roadmap item says 'every decision recorded as a routing audit event'. The plan should either state explicitly that failed routing attempts are not audited and specify the structured WARNING they emit (with task type, policy checksum, and reason), or add a non-transactional failure event so operators can see why routing keeps falling back to static.

findings.description: The local fallback algorithm is underspecified in three places that affect determinism tests: (a) whether `routing.yaml` `rules` and `defaults.phase_dispatch_modes` are evaluated locally or only the `fallback` order is used, which decides what `matched_rule_ids` and `dispatch_mode` contain; (b) how one lane is chosen when several agents.yaml lanes share the caller's provider type (claude_code and codex each have a local and a cloud lane), including the tiebreak after `location_order`/`isolation_order`; (c) what the helper returns when the provider has no lane at all. Spec scenario 'Coordinator is unreachable' only pins the provenance flags. State the selection order and tiebreak (e.g. `agent_id` ascending) and the no-lane failure so tests can be written first.

findings.existing_code:
The response detail distinguishes
            routing-registry-unavailable, no-feasible-routing-assignment, and
            routing-durability-unavailable.
findings.description: The service currently raises `RoutingUnavailableError("no feasible model-routing candidate")` (api.py line 311) and the coordination_mcp test asserts that exact detail string (tests/model_routing/test_api.py lines 290-296). Renaming the detail to `no-feasible-routing-assignment` is a wire change on the existing dg-00 operation that D1 describes as unchanged. Callers via `resolve_archetype_for_phase` are safe because any non-200 falls back, but the plan should state the detail rename and list the dg-00 tests to update, so it is not treated as a regression during review.

findings.existing_code:
- **WHEN** `routing.yaml` contains an unknown field, unsupported schema version, invalid
  enum, duplicate rule ID, or reference to an unconfigured phase dispatch default
findings.description: 'Reference to an unconfigured phase' has no stated source of truth. `phase_dispatch_modes` in contracts/config/routing.schema.json accepts any key, so the loader must cross-check against something (presumably `archetypes.yaml` phase_mapping). Name the source, because the skills-side fallback helper must apply the same check from the checkout and both loaders must agree on what a configured phase is.

`Candidate` carries both a top-level `agent_id` and `assignment.agent_id`, and a per-candidate `provenance`, while design D6 says candidates carry only `assignment` and provenance lives at the response top level. Pick one: either drop `Candidate.agent_id`/`Candidate.provenance` from the contract, or state in D6 that `selected.provenance` is populated and alternatives' `provenance` is null. Otherwise the parity test has no single answer for what a successful response contains.

The four packages form a strict chain, so nothing runs in parallel. The skills-side half of wp-transports-fallback (`routing_fallback.py`, `test_routing_fallback.py`, and the bridge helper) depends only on the routing.yaml schema and agents.yaml, not on the coordinator service. Splitting it into a package that depends only on wp-contract-config lets it run alongside wp-policy-service, leaving only the coordination_mcp/http_proxy mirror in the package that waits for the service.

findings.existing_code:
Multiple lanes may project the same catalog
model, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.
findings.description: D5 handles ordering for duplicate lane/model pairs but not their effect on the unchanged dg-00 exploration and normalisation. Each lane projecting the same catalog model becomes a separate `CandidateInput`, so that model contributes multiple entries to `choose()` (more exploration draws) and to the min-max cost/latency normalisation. State whether that weighting is accepted or whether exploration should be keyed by catalog identity, and add it to task 3.4's compatibility check.
